abstract_read.exact_text: How well can a dealer forecast the largest absolute recorded net position before a reporting horizon ends? Such forecasts motivate evaluating a monitoring input for the measured position series. We compare historical peak constructions with ridge quantile regression and local quantiles on a market maker's FX client-flow series and a weekly Treasury-dealer aggregate. The common target includes the observed issue position and uses completed training labels. First, six-record FX regression lowers matched-history pinball loss by 14.77%, while breaches rise from 360 to 376. Second, the Treasury primary deteriorates by 50.79%, with breaches rising from 28 to 54. Third, lower pinball loss often accompanies more breach occasions. The evidence is specific to the inspected records, stipulated score and source-measurement conventions.

supporting_exact_text.exact_sentence_or_paragraph: Dealers absorb customer order imbalances while managing inventory risk and scarce balance-sheet capacity. Inventory affects optimal dealer pricing (Ho and Stoll, 1981), FX dealing (Lyons, 1995), and observed inventory adjustment in dealership markets (Hansch, Naik and Viswanathan, 1998). Treasury intermediation likewise depends on dealer capacity (Duffie et al., 2023). A forecast of the maximum recorded position magnitude over a future horizon may support monitoring of the measured position: an endpoint can return toward its starting value after an intervening large position. Translating that monitoring signal into a particular margin or financing decision requires the corresponding contractual and balance-sheet inputs.

We ask whether mature conditional estimators improve forecasts of an absolute sampled-position peak relative to simple historical constructions. Every procedure predicts the same upper quantile of the same response on common issue origins. The historical alternatives use past headrooms, paths translated to the current signed position, or native peaks floored at the observed current magnitude. The conditional alternatives use ridge quantile regression, nearest-neighbor quantiles and scaled nearest-neighbor quantiles.

The matched-history FX regression comparison lowers mean loss by 14.77%, but increases breaches from 360 to 376. The original FX primary uses a different historical window and lowers loss by 12.66%. The separately declared Treasury primary deteriorates by 50.79%, with 54 rather than 28 breaches. Short-history FX regression also deteriorates at the longer horizon; a Treasury neighbor gain reverses on the sparse grid. These adverse outcomes are central findings.

The paper makes three contributions. First, it places established forecasting engines and historical constructions on a common completed-peak response with an explicit issue-known floor. Second, it controls completed-label pools and update schedules and retains the complete favorable and adverse model menu. Third, it documents how score, breach frequency, report coherence and fixed-report preferences can disagree across two financial measurement processes. The contribution is an application and model-validation benchmark using mature methods.

supporting_exact_text.exact_sentence_or_paragraph: Wisniewski, Lindsay and Lindsay (2020) and the net-position forecasting chapter of Wisniewski (2024) are the closest empirical lineage. They already study conditional, neighbor and normalized endpoint forecasts on the FX source family, using lagged positions and calendar information. Here the response is a single upper quantile of a future absolute sampled maximum, including the current magnitude. Marginal endpoint intervals and their averaged losses address a different functional; the present comparison fits the established engines directly to completed peak labels.

Financial path extrema have a substantial prior literature. MaxVaR evaluates worst intermediate mark-to-market loss (Boudoukh et al., 2004). Liao and Theodosopoulos (2005) study the timing of mark-to-market for collateralized contingent credit exposure. Van den Hoogen (2017) models a conditional intraday liquidity buffer through the maximum cumulative payment deficit; Petrunia, Sabetti and Voia (2019) study a cross-participant end-of-day debit maximum. Arjani, Li and Sabetti (2020) forecast remaining-day liquidity-demand ratios. These targets clarify the specific contribution of a sampled net-position envelope.

Regression quantiles (Koenker and Bassett, 1978), sequential neighbor quantiles (Biau and Patra, 2011), conditional historical filtering (Hull and White, 1998; Barone-Adesi et al., 1999), and quantile scoring (Gneiting, 2011) supply the mature methods. Quantile forests (Meinshausen, 2006), CAViaR (Engle and Manganelli, 2004), sequential conformal prediction (Xu and Xie, 2023), trajectory calibration (Zhou, Lindemann and Sesia, 2024) and expected-shortfall curves (Sözen, 2026) are further relevant alternatives. The executed estimator menu is deliberately bounded.

The resulting distinction is the measured peak response, known issue floor, completed-label timing, controlled history/update comparisons and qualified aggregate application. The benchmark measures how these mature procedures behave on the specified task; its supporting finite geometry explains construction differences.

supporting_exact_text.exact_sentence_or_paragraph: The executed QR specifications perform poorly on the weekly Treasury task. Their 25 level coordinates span the current observation through 24 weeks of history. The two hour coordinates, two weekday coordinates and gap indicator are exactly constant on this weekly source. Training-only centering makes those five columns exactly zero, so they provide no predictive variation and are not a demonstrated mechanism of overfitting. The original nominal design has 33 predictors plus an intercept, or 34 coefficients, with at most 28 varying columns and 29 potentially predictive coefficients before other collinearity, against W=52 overlapping training labels in the shorter history. All four Treasury penalty selections are menu endpoints. Its 52 validation origins contain at most 3 disjoint H24 label paths, a path count rather than an effective-sample-size estimate. Correlated lag levels, overlapping labels, restricted tuning, target dynamics and reporting composition remain competing explanations. Neither the parsimonious sensitivity nor the aggregate panel separates those mechanisms.

The four-predictor sensitivity uses B, signed N and short/long increment RMS, with validation penalties {0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10}. It lowers loss against the original QR in 5 of 8 cells and against matched F in 3 cells. In the Treasury primary cell its loss change is -32.2% relative to the original QR and 2.17% relative to F. All adverse cells remain in Table 8. The exercise changes features and the penalty menu jointly, so it measures a parsimonious specification sensitivity rather than identifying a feature-only cause or rehabilitating the original primary.

The contrast between the sources concerns a separately fitted procedure family: each source receives its own transforms, coefficient estimates, temporal scales and validation selection. The Treasury deterioration is an accuracy failure of the executed QR specifications. The exploratory AR comparison shows that the observed Treasury loss ranking differs across the executed families.

The FX evaluation interval was previously inspected, and the subsequent robustness analyses are post-result / exploratory. These records do not restore a compatible unseen dealer sample. Treasury is a downloaded-vintage, economic-date aggregate replay rather than an original-release public-information backtest; cross-dealer netting, valuation and composition distinguish it from an individual dealer's book.

Shared histories, overlapping labels, finite validation and investigator selection limit statistical generalization. The known floor can create an outcome atom: a valid upper quantile need not have exactly the nominal strict-breach probability. Numerical acceptance supplies no conditional-coverage guarantee. The horizon-specific mature scenario sets differ, so a zero observed crossing count cannot establish general coherence.

Stipulated shortfall/excess weights are not observed financing prices. Quotes, fills, hedges, book decomposition, collateral and cash flows would be required to map this passive envelope into an operational inventory, margin or funding policy. This study evaluates forecasts, not such interventions; Avellaneda and Stoikov (2008) provide a distinct active inventory-sensitive quoting framework.

Further alternatives include CAViaR, sequential conformal procedures, richer mean or volatility dynamics, and canonical innovation-tail conditional EVT. The fixed FHS, QRF and peak-POT additions in Appendix L extend the executed menu, with their failures and resource bounds retained. Same mature-label pools and update schedules improve procedural comparability while leaving different feature lookbacks, model assumptions and estimation rules. Compatible new dealer observations and decision-linked inputs remain necessary for broader portability.

A post-result / exploratory selected-fit readback examines the Treasury C2 menu boundary directly (Appendix I). At λ=10, standardized response-normalized slope norms range from 0.001497 to 0.01937. Removing slopes while keeping each fitted intercept changes capacity by a mean absolute 136.8–832.3 source USD millions across the four cells. Relative to the lower empirical headroom-quantile report I, observed loss is 0.2432–2.192% lower; this descriptive difference has no dedicated selection-adjusted test. The fits have small normalized slopes and high headroom correlation with I, but are not identical to I or F. A boundary penalty and high capacity correlation do not by themselves demonstrate zero feature value. Three of the four C2 cells still have higher loss than F.

The expanded aggregate panel strengthens the negative transport finding but does not isolate its mechanism. Features and tuning menus, finite sample size, target behavior and reporting-regime changes can all matter. Downloaded cross-era histories are not original-release vintages; metadata/provenance for each key are retained. A prospective public-release protocol freezes the four procedures and selected historical-validation penalties before future issue artifacts. The first planned new release is after the protocol freeze, rather than retroactively labeling the already published October 14 observation as unseen. Because the release clock lags economic dates, the target includes prediction of unpublished measurements, with a nowcast/forecast mixture. A dated local amendment fixes future path values at their first actual capture and logs later revisions separately; operational capture and missing-week handling still require a bound adapter (Appendix K). Results await prior timestamped report issuance and target publication; no live prospective validation is claimed.

supporting_exact_text.exact_sentence_or_paragraph: Mature conditional estimators change the historical ranking on the sampled FX peak task, while the Treasury regression primary deteriorates. Matched-history FX H6 QR lowers mean loss by 14.77% and raises breaches from 360 to 376; the Treasury primary raises loss by 50.79% and breaches from 28 to 54. Short-history QR deterioration and the sparse-grid Treasury neighbor reversal remain central adverse findings. The exploratory AR, rank, preference and coherence comparisons show why score improvements, breach frequency and report shape should be evaluated together. The study contributes a controlled application and model-validation benchmark for measured position peaks. Its next evidential step is compatible new financial observations and an explicit decision mapping.
The exploratory 12-series extension also finds higher loss than F in 45/48 QR33 cells and 37/48 parsimonious cells, further limiting general performance claims.

findings.exact_sentence: Every procedure predicts the same upper quantile of the same response on common issue origins.
findings.why_substantive: A common evaluation response/score does not imply every benchmark estimates the same statistical functional. The later L construction uses an absolute endpoint .975quantile to produce a population upper bound on peak breach under independent symmetric increments. It need not equal the peak .95quantile even with an ideal population oracle. This universal sentence therefore overstates the common-functional claim once L is included.
findings.analytic_check_not_experiment: For one step with zero start and a continuous nondegenerate symmetric increment, peak=absolute increment. Luses its .975quantile, while the exact peak .95quantile is lower. No new simulation, financial parameter, output or statistical calculation is involved.
